To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a fast Fourier transform-acclerated integral-equations based algorithm is developed for the analysis of electromagnetic wave interactions with planar structures residing above or inside an arbitrarily lossy half-space.
a fast Fourier transform-acclerated mixed-potential integral-equation based time-domain solution of scattering from planar structures above or inside a half-space environment is developed.
a novel integral equation formulation is presented for the transient scattering from planars residing above a potentially lossy half-space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the solution of time-domain integral equations in the mixed-potential form.
the development of fast solution techniques for transient electromagnetic scattering problems in half-space environments.
the development of fast and efficient time-domain integral-equation solvers for analyzing electromagnetic wave interactions in lossy half-space environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithm is the most efficient time-domain method to date for analyzing transient wave interactions with planar structures. 6 refs., 7 figs.

, for the class of problems addressed, the proposed algorithm is a viable, efficient, and accurate solution to the mixed-potential integral-equation formulation of the time-domain half-space scattering problem.
the proposed scheme is an efficient and accurate algorithm for analyzing transient scattering from planars residing in a half-space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a fast time-domain algorithm for analyzing transient electromagnetic scattering from planar objects above or in a potentially lossy half-space.
the proposed algorithm provides an efficient means for analyzing transient scattering from planer PEC structures in a half-space environment.
a mixed-potential integral equation (MPIE)-based algorithm has been developed to solve transient electromagnetic scattering from planar structures above and inside a potentially loss half-space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fast solution to mixed-potential integral equations can be obtained by pre-computing the time-domain half-space Greens functions from their frequency-domain representations.
a time-domain solution of a half-space problem can be obtained in the same amount of CPU time and with the same memory resources as the frequency-domain solution.

the time-domain integral-equation based analysis of electromagnetic wave interactions with planar structures residing above or inside an inhomogeneous dielectric half-space can be performed with computational efficiency and memory usage that are similar to those of classical time-marching schemes.
